meta.label: 7개 구단 전체 후보·티어·포지션 순위 공개 · 검수 중
meta.note: All 120 candidate players across ten positions registered for seven verified 2001-02 UEFA-qualified clubs. Tier grades S–D, within-position ranks and 4-2-3-1 Best XI are 1st-pass draft subject to three-season audit. Sources: 2000-01 BDFutbol club lineup/starts. 0 dates of birth intentionally left null instead of inventing dates.
meta.qualificationNotes: Real Zaragoza qualified for 2001-02 UEFA Cup through 2000-01 Copa del Rey title despite finishing 17th in league. Villareal and Malaga did not actually enter 2001 Intertoto; the Spanish federation withdrew two places in June 2001, confirmed by contemporaneous UEFA announcement.
meta.historicalCrestPolicy: Modern/reference badges are inherited from 1999-00 season data; this stage does not establish exact 2000-01 artwork.

gkSelectionReview.notes: Reina 18 league starts and Dutruel 15 are Barcelona rotating pair; Mallorca Miki Garro chosen with 5 league starts (Roa 4); Zaragoza César Láinez started the cup final despite 3 league starts; Cañizares only Valencia qualifying keeper with 37 league starts.
gkSelectionReview.note: Previous 13 GK candidates retained, tiers and ranks now preliminary.

tierProposal.assessmentNote: Initial qualitative 2000-01 league impact, 1999-00 continuity and 1998-99 context; historical 3-year player-by-player verification still incomplete. Club league placement not counted as direct tier score.

positionalRanking.scope: 1..N separately in each primary position; no global rank; player grades and ranking tentative

bestXiReview.label: 2000–01 4-2-3-1 1차 선정안
bestXiReview.notes: 4-2-3-1 selected as a period-representative lineup, not statistically verified league-wide modal formation. Rivaldo plays CAM as second-striker/advanced-playmaker eligible under flexible user instruction. Each XI player is #1 in their respective ranked primary slot except the second CB, who is #2; Best XI and primary-position allocation subject to correction.

legacyComparison.source: 1999-2009 La Liga.xlsx, sheet 00-01, pre-existing stage1 normalized extraction

excludedAnachronisms.name: Zinedine Zidane
excludedAnachronisms.reason: joined Real Madrid in July 2001; 2001-02, not 2000-01

excludedAnachronisms.name: Francisco Farinós
excludedAnachronisms.reason: moved from Valencia to Inter in June 2000; not a Valencia player in 2000-01

historicalStandingsCorrection.legacyOrigin: The legacy spreadsheet faithfully reproduces the English Wikipedia 2000–01 La Liga table (Espanyol 15W-7D-16L, 52 points); this is NOT a manual copying error.
historicalStandingsCorrection.discrepancy: English Wikipedia lists 52 points (15-7-16). Spanish Wikipedia, original LFP 2000–01 annual report, Espanyol official club retrospective, BDFutbol, FBref and RSSSF all list 50 points (14-8-16).
historicalStandingsCorrection.resolution: Retain site record of 50 points; mark contradiction as source inconsistency, not user spreadsheet error.

legacyComparison.significantDifferences: Some player primary positions and within-position ranks differ from legacy rankings; original legacy spreadsheet did not carry S-D tiers, so tiers cannot be benchmarked.
legacyComparison.reviewDisposition: Keep the currently published 120-person working draft, with no change to player pool, provisional tiers, positions, ranks or XI.
legacyComparison.verificationScope: Compared against preexisting normalized workbook extract; direct original binary not accessible in this turn.

meta.reviewDisposition: Working roster retained after legacy comparison; preliminary grades and XI still pending full three-season statistical audit
